parts.visual:
Old software: You request a demo, a salesman calls you in a suit, negotiates a $10,000 contract, and then you finally see the software. 
PLG software (like Slack or Zoom): You just go to the website, download it instantly for free, start using it with your team, and when you hit a limit, the software itself prompts you to enter a credit card.

The PLG Revolution:
1. Product-Led Growth: A strategy where the product itself is the primary driver of acquisition, expansion, and retention. You do not hire an army of salesmen; you engineer the software to sell itself.
2. End-User Era: In the 90s, software was sold to the CEO (Top-Down). Today, software is adopted by the junior employees (Bottom-Up) who just start using it, and eventually force the CEO to pay for the enterprise tier.
parts.audio: In a Product-Led Growth company, the product is your best marketing team, your best sales rep, and your best customer success agent. The code does the convincing, not humans.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'Top-Down Sales' and 'Bottom-Up' (PLG) adoption?
options: Top-Down means the servers are on the roof.

Top-Down means selling to the Boss, who forces the employees to use a clunky system. Bottom-Up means individual employees fall in love with a beautiful app, use it for free, and it spreads virally through the office until the Boss is forced to buy it.
questions.correct_answer: Top-Down means selling to the Boss, who forces the employees to use a clunky system. Bottom-Up means individual employees fall in love with a beautiful app, use it for free, and it spreads virally through the office until the Boss is forced to buy it.
questions.explanation: Slack destroyed Microsoft's early chat tools using the Bottom-Up Trojan Horse.

questions.question: Listen to the PLG expert explaining 'Time to Value' (TTV). Why is a low TTV critical for this model?
questions.tts_text: If someone downloads your app and has to read a 10-page manual to understand it, they will uninstall it in 30 seconds. In PLG, the user must experience a 'Aha! Moment' within the first 60 seconds of opening the app, or you lose them forever.
options: Without a salesperson holding their hand, the software's UI must instantly deliver value. A low 'Time to Value' means the user realizes exactly why the product is amazing almost immediately, creating instant addiction.
questions.correct_answer: Without a salesperson holding their hand, the software's UI must instantly deliver value. A low 'Time to Value' means the user realizes exactly why the product is amazing almost immediately, creating instant addiction.

questions.question: How does a PLG company use 'Product-Qualified Leads' (PQLs) instead of traditional Marketing Leads?
options: They ask the user to take a test.

Instead of cold-calling someone who downloaded a PDF, the sales team only calls users who have already used the free product heavily (e.g., 'This user sent 500 messages this week'). The product data tells the sales team exactly who is ready to buy.
questions.correct_answer: Instead of cold-calling someone who downloaded a PDF, the sales team only calls users who have already used the free product heavily (e.g., 'This user sent 500 messages this week'). The product data tells the sales team exactly who is ready to buy.
questions.explanation: Don't sell to strangers. Sell to power-users.

questions.question: What is the biggest risk of attempting a PLG strategy?
options: Terrible Onboarding. If your product is highly complex (like cybersecurity infrastructure), users cannot simply 'download it and figure it out'. PLG only works if the product is incredibly intuitive. Complex products still require human sales engineers.
questions.correct_answer: Terrible Onboarding. If your product is highly complex (like cybersecurity infrastructure), users cannot simply 'download it and figure it out'. PLG only works if the product is incredibly intuitive. Complex products still require human sales engineers.
questions.explanation: You cannot self-serve an airplane engine.
